_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); hotel signals

pit_profile.why: Marriott: 'Consistent with our focus on management, franchising, and licensing, we own very few of our lodging properties'; 'We are a worldwide operator, franchisor, and licensor of hotel, residential, and timeshare properties in 133 countries and territories under 30 brand names'; 'COVID-19 has had a material detrimental impact on our business and financial results, and such impact could continue and may worsen for an unknown period of time'; 'Worldwide comparable systemwide constant dollar RevPAR declined 23 percent in the 2020 first quarter, 84 percent in the 2020 second quarter, 66 percent in the 2020 third quarter, and 64 percent in the 2020 fourth quarter, compared to the same periods in 2019'; 'we expect that there will not be a significant rebound in travel and lodging demand until there is widespread distribution of effective vaccines'; 'Even after COVID-19 subsides or effective vaccines or treatments become widely available, our business, markets, growth prospects and business model could continue to be materially impacted or altered'; 'Our industry is highly competitive, which may impact our ability to compete successfully for guests with other hotel properties and home sharing or rental services'; 'Economic downturns and other global, national, and regional conditions could further impact our financial results and growth'; and 'An increase in the use of third-party Internet services to book online hotel reservations could adversely impact our business' (its own FY2020 10-K): a hotel management and franchise system whose fees follow the revenues and profits of its hotels through the economy, by its own account; no disruption theme is live for it

classification.quality_note: Marriott: 'Consistent with our focus on management, franchising, and licensing, we own very few of our lodging properties'; 'We are a worldwide operator, franchisor, and licensor of hotel, residential, and timeshare properties in 133 countries and territories under 30 brand names'; 'COVID-19 has had a material detrimental impact on our business and financial results, and such impact could continue and may worsen for an unknown period of time'; 'Worldwide comparable systemwide constant dollar RevPAR declined 23 percent in the 2020 first quarter, 84 percent in the 2020 second quarter, 66 percent in the 2020 third quarter, and 64 percent in the 2020 fourth quarter, compared to the same periods in 2019'; 'we expect that there will not be a significant rebound in travel and lodging demand until there is widespread distribution of effective vaccines'; 'Even after COVID-19 subsides or effective vaccines or treatments become widely available, our business, markets, growth prospects and business model could continue to be materially impacted or altered'; 'Our industry is highly competitive, which may impact our ability to compete successfully for guests with other hotel properties and home sharing or rental services'; 'Economic downturns and other global, national, and regional conditions could further impact our financial results and growth'; and 'An increase in the use of third-party Internet services to book online hotel reservations could adversely impact our business' (its own FY2020 10-K): a hotel management and franchise system whose fees follow the revenues and profits of its hotels through the economy, by its own account; no disruption theme is live for it. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.41x; +100% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +2.03; conservative 2yr +126%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -29.4%/yr (worst year FY11-FY19, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +96.7%/yr (Q3 fees + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr ex-FY20 median

BULL.desc: EPS +96.7%/yr (FY11-FY19 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +96.7%/yr (best 2-yr run FY11-FY19); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: MAR (retrospective, 2022-01-28) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.41x (74.9% downside to Bear $40 / +183.0% upside to Bull $451) | Adj composite 3.55 vs market 1.52: gap +2.03 [UNDERVALUED] | +100% above the EPP floor $80 (21x FY21E $3.80) | Conservative 2-yr case: +125.9% total (+63.0%/yr) | At 41.9x FY21E the 15% hurdle price $211 sits at or below the BASE case; North American RevPAR +258.3% in Q3 2021, forward fee revenue +95.5% (no FY21 fee guide, Q3 2021 fees); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
